## F12.client-support — Client support

SDK sessions that configure MCP servers can also expose MCP prompts as commands. ## F12.transports — Transports

Definition: stdio, HTTP, SSE and similar.
- claude-code [supported, unverified] MCP servers can use stdio, SSE or HTTP transports. A local stdio server runs as a process Claude Code starts from the `command` and `args` fields of its configuration. An SDK MCP server for custom tools runs in-process inside the application, not as a separate process. `claude mcp login` works for HTTP, SSE and claude.ai connector servers. | ev: E-claude-code-00517, E-claude-code-09463, E-claude-code-00318, E-claude-code-06997
- codex-cli [supported, verified] The `add` subcommand of `codex mcp` supports both stdio and streamable HTTP transports. A stdio server has a launcher command and runs as a local process started by that command; a streamable HTTP server has an endpoint URL. | ev: E-codex-cli-01156, E-codex-cli-00588, E-codex-cli-00589, E-codex-cli-03827
- copilot-cli [supported, unverified] Copilot CLI supports both local and remote MCP servers. Local or STDIO servers start a local process and communicate over stdin/stdout; remote servers are HTTP/SSE. The CLI accepts stdio, streamable-http, and sse MCP transport names. | ev: E-copilot-cli-02085, E-copilot-cli-02418, E-copilot-cli-01030, E-copilot-cli-03814
- copilot-vscode [supported, unverified] Standard I/O (stdio) servers are the most common type for locally-run MCP servers. For HTTP servers VS Code first tries the HTTP Stream transport and falls back to SSE; SSE has legacy support. HTTP servers can also listen on Unix sockets (`unix:///path/to/server.sock`) or Windows named pipes (`pipe:///pipe/named-pipe`). | ev: E-copilot-vscode-00621, E-copilot-vscode-00622, E-copilot-vscode-00052, E-copilot-vscode-00623
- cursor [partial, verified] Custom MCP servers for cloud agents can use HTTP or stdio transport. Local servers are configured with `command` and `args`. MCP servers can be written in any language that can print to `stdout` or serve an HTTP endpoint. The Python SDK HTTP server config has `type: Literal["http", "sse"]`, default "http". | limit: For cloud-agent custom MCP servers, "SSE and `mcp-remote` are not supported" (E-cursor-02121), while the Python SDK config type accepts "http" or "sse" (E-cursor-01214); the quotes do not reconcile the two. | ev: E-cursor-02121, E-cursor-01214, E-cursor-00611, E-cursor-03345
- gemini-cli [partial, verified] Stdio transport spawns a subprocess and communicates via stdin/stdout; SSE transport connects to Server-Sent Events endpoints; `httpUrl` is the URL of an MCP server that uses streamable HTTP transport. | limit: Admin-required MCP servers: 'Required servers only support remote transports (`sse`, `http`).' | ev: E-gemini-cli-02215, E-gemini-cli-02216, E-gemini-cli-00729, E-gemini-cli-01058
- grok-build [supported, verified] The url field of an [mcp_servers.‹name›] entry is an HTTP/SSE MCP endpoint. | ev: E-grok-build-00077
- grok-bot [supported, verified] A Command server runs on whichever computer the conversation uses. For a custom server that needs secrets, the docs say to choose Remote HTTPS. | ev: E-grok-bot-01018, E-grok-bot-01020

## F12.tool-filtering — Tool filtering and naming

Definition: How MCP tools are named, allowed or hidden.
- claude-code [supported, verified] MCP tools are named `mcp__‹server-name›__‹tool-name›`. Deny rules support tool-name globs: `*` matches every tool and `mcp__*` matches every MCP tool across all servers. An agent's `disallowedTools` also accepts `mcp__server` or `mcp__server__*` to remove every tool from that server. By default, MCP tool schemas stay deferred and load on demand via tool search. | ev: E-claude-code-00403, E-claude-code-00453, E-claude-code-00824, E-claude-code-07370
- codex-cli [supported, verified] An MCP server's tools can be limited with an allow list of tool names (`enabled_tools`) and a deny list applied after it. Individual MCP tools can use `approval_mode = "prompt"`. Hook matchers match the MCP tool name, such as `mcp__filesystem__read_file`. | ev: E-codex-cli-00601, E-codex-cli-00602, E-codex-cli-01827, E-codex-cli-01129
- copilot-cli [supported, unverified] Naming an MCP server alone allows or denies all of its tools; a tool name registered with the server, in parentheses, scopes to one tool. --allow-tool accepts patterns such as MyMCP(create_issue). --add-github-mcp-tool adds a GitHub MCP server tool beyond the default CLI subset (repeatable; * for all). Tool search loads extra tools only when needed. | ev: E-copilot-cli-00047, E-copilot-cli-00500, E-copilot-cli-00933, E-copilot-cli-00190
- copilot-vscode [supported, unverified] Configure Tools in the chat input lists an MCP server's tools and lets you toggle specific tools on or off; MCP tools can be enabled and configured with the tools picker. A custom agent's `tools` field can include all tools of an MCP server with `‹server name›/*`. An experimental setting groups tools into virtual tools activated on demand, to go beyond the limit of 128 tools for a chat request. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-01675, E-copilot-vscode-00120, E-copilot-vscode-00593, E-copilot-vscode-00059
- cursor [supported, unverified] CLI permissions control which MCP tools the agent can run, using `server` (from `mcp.json`) and `tool` name with `*` wildcards. Allowlist entries (`mcpAllowlist`) use `server:tool` syntax for tools that may run without approval. Tools can be toggled on or off by clicking the tool name in the chat panel's tools list. Hook matchers address MCP tools as `MCP:‹tool_name›`. | ev: E-cursor-00334, E-cursor-00550, E-cursor-01446, E-cursor-00847
- gemini-cli [supported, unverified] Restricting tools within an MCP server is done using the `includeTools` and `excludeTools` properties. The `--allowed-mcp-server-names` flag takes allowed MCP server names (comma-separated or multiple flags). An MCP tool's registered name is potentially prefixed. In the policy engine, `mcp_server_*` matches any tool from a specific MCP server. | ev: E-gemini-cli-01506, E-gemini-cli-00011, E-gemini-cli-00978, E-gemini-cli-00808
- grok-build [supported, unverified] MCP tools are available alongside the built-in ones, namespaced as ‹server›__‹tool›.
